finalReview.reasoning: Verified byte-level invariants first-hand (src/args.js currently has exactly 134 CR bytes, test/args.test.js exactly 179, matching the stated pre-diff floor — I could not re-count post-diff since I'm read-only and won't materialize the patched file, but the diff's added lines are ASCII substitutions inside existing hunks with no visible corruption). Confirmed MINIMUM_MAP_BUDGET is already exported from src/repo-map.js (line 372) so the args.js import is valid and non-circular (repo-map.js imports nothing from args.js). Confirmed bin/loop.js's main() catches parseArgs() throws, writes 'arg error: <message>' to stderr and sets process.exitCode = 2 before parseArgs ever touches the filesystem, so the new bin-level spawn test is a genuine, well-founded process-level assertion. Read the full buildRepoMap body (src/repo-map.js lines 374-687) and traced finalizeRung's wiring by hand: for the 'detailed', 'collapsed', and 'collapsedNoSymbols' rungs, renderedPaths/withheldPaths are built incrementally inside the real per-directory/per-entry loop (every entry ends up in exactly one of the two sets via actual control flow), so reconcileRepoMapCoverage is a genuine bidirectional check there. But for the final compactFallback rung, renderCompactFallback now returns `declaredPaths: new Set(entries.map(e => e.path))` — built from the exact same `entries` array, with the exact same map expression, as the outer `classifiedPaths` used inside reconcileRepoMapCoverage. Two Sets constructed identically from the identical input array are always equal; this means the coverage check on the last-resort rung can never throw, regardless of what renderCompactFallback actually renders or omits. That is precisely the 'bare count equality' (here, a bare identity) the task and settled rule 5 explicitly forbid ('Coverage checking cannot pass by counting; membership is checked in both directions' — this rung checks nothing). It's also the rung most likely to accumulate future accounting bugs (it's the emergency fallback, exercised by existing tests at test/repo-map.test.js:133 and :252), and this change gives it zero protection while appearing, on a shallow read, to have the same safeguard as the other three rungs. The new unit tests only exercise reconcileRepoMapCoverage in isolation with hand-built Sets, so they don't surface this — the tautology is invisible at the test level. This is the task's central deliverable ('coverage reconciles bidirectionally'), and it's fake for 1 of the 4 return paths, so I won't land it as-is.
